reader.model: 8B board filter + Qwen3-VL-235B reader + source-edge rejection
reader.prompt: Examine this crop from an NBHL ball-hockey recording. First determine whether it actually shows an electronic sports scoreboard. Advertising signs, rink names, notices, spectators, clothing and dark/blank crops are not scoreboards. If it is a scoreboard, read only fully visible digits with identifiable labels. The home and guest/visitor score labels must establish which score is which; do not guess from position alone. A partially cropped board can have null fields. Do not infer hidden digits, score, period, clock, team names, final result or a goal. Return JSON only: {"is_scoreboard":boolean,"home":integer or null,"guest":integer or null,"period":integer or null,"clock":"M:SS or seconds.tenths or null","evidence":"short visible evidence or reason for uncertainty"}. For non-scoreboards return false and null for every field. For a scoreboard clock use a JSON null when unreadable, not the word null.

guard.policy: Reject the whole crop when its grounding rectangle lies within 1 percent of any source-frame border. Fixed post-audit geometry rule, no threshold sweep. Can reject readable boards. Interior crops can still be partial or wrong.
guard.scope: Development diagnostic motivated by partial scoreboard errors.

reference_comparison.scope: Conditional comparison on 59 previously reviewed board timestamps. These are not an exhaustive label set for every frame in the recording.

timeline.provenance: Automatic postprocessing of video-only board readings. No official game events used.
timeline.limitations: Two agreeing views within 180 seconds confirm a score state; this is a heuristic. Large jumps and decreasing scores need review. Goal search intervals add a 20-second delay allowance and are not guaranteed event bounds. Clock coverage is sparse; matching stopped endpoints do not prove the entire interval was stopped. No full-game final score or player stats are inferred.

policy: Reject malformed values. Combine agreeing crop fields within each timestamp, suppress conflicting fields, then require agreement at two distinct timestamps for a score state. No official record or event timestamps enter recognition or timeline construction.
limitations: Development diagnostic with assistant reference labels. Unreviewed accepted board crops can be false positives. Two temporal readings can repeat the same error. Automatic score states and goal candidates remain unverified; no shots, assists, shooters, possession, complete final scores, or time on floor are inferred.
